description: Bringing the energy from the silicon to the real world, from infinity to beyond. Helping Vienna to discover the hidden data of the sky.
summary:
Procedural Space helps researchers decide where to look in a sky full of data. We built a flexible research platform around standardized Python extractors: researchers define what matters for their question, and the analysis pipeline turns observations into priority values and ranked hotspot overlays.

From a promising region, researchers can open real SPHEREx image cutouts, blink between visits, follow the timeline, and inspect spectral samples with wavelengths, units, dates, and quality information. Different research questions can use different extractors through the same interface.

For the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, we connect programmable search with visual inspection of NASA's infrared observations, helping researchers move from a research question to focused, inspectable evidence.
details:
Your research question. Your extractor. A focused search.

Astronomical archives are too large to inspect observation by observation. Procedural Space connects researcher-defined analysis with an interactive sky map and the evidence behind each result.

How it works

Researchers can write Python or “vibe code” custom extractors, using a shared interface and templates. The pipeline converts their analysis into priority values, ranked hotspots and heatmap overlays.

Extractors can be tailored to questions such as H₂O and CO₂ signatures, custom absorption-line analysis, periodicity detection, motion and variability. Lithium-content studies can incorporate suitable complementary spectra. Each analysis depends on the available wavelength coverage, resolution and data quality. The public prototype demonstrates the workflow with prepared examples and analysis controls.

From hotspot to evidence

Open genuine SPHEREx cutouts, blink between visits, follow observation dates and inspect spectral samples with wavelengths, units, quality information and provenance. Real examples, including Barnard’s Star, connect programmable search to visual evidence for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

Built with

Python scientific processing, a JavaScript web interface, background workers and NASA/IPAC IRSA data. SPHEREx observations are supported by catalogue and historical context, with a 2MASS reference sky.

SI assistance and credits

Claude and OpenAI Codex assisted with research, code, analysis, writing, design, slides and video editing. Presenter footage is the team’s original recording. The team wrote the script and directed the video. Astronomical imagery and measurements come from the credited datasets. Ideation was completely human.

SPHEREx: NASA/JPL-Caltech and IPAC. 2MASS: University of Massachusetts/IPAC, funded by NASA and NSF; HiPS imagery via CDS and IRSA. WISE/AllWISE and CatWISE: NASA/IPAC IRSA. Catalogue context: ESA Gaia, CDS SIMBAD and AAVSO VSX. Stars and constellations: d3-celestial / Olaf Frohn.
